themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 7 this week versus a 1.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (409% increase, z-score 6.56), suggesting either organized tree vandalism or construction activity stripping the district's urban canopy.
evidence: 7 illegal tree damage complaints filed this week vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (409% spike, z-score 6.56)
First statistically significant spike in this category in the 90-day dataset
Aligns with active construction permits (697 DOB filings in 90 days, including 8 full demolitions)
reporting_angles: Are contractors demolishing or altering buildings without proper tree protection permits? Interview Parks Dept enforcement.
Site visits to tree damage hotspots to photograph and geo-map the damage pattern—is it concentrated on specific blocks or development zones?

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Crisis in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints exploded to 6 last week versus a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score 11.62), indicating widespread building code violations or deferred maintenance affecting tenant access and mobility.
evidence: 6 elevator complaints filed last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 11.62)
Second-most extreme spike in the dataset by z-score after illegal posting
Overlaps with heat/hot water as top complaint type (2,193 complaints over 90 days), suggesting broader building maintenance failures
reporting_angles: Interview affected tenants (especially elderly and disabled residents) about how broken elevators strand them in walk-ups; identify specific buildings with repeat violations.
FOIA DOB violation records for this district: which landlords have the most open elevator violation tickets and why haven't they been resolved?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 5 last week from a 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (3900% increase, z-score 14.74, highest severity spike in dataset), likely signaling coordinated poster campaigns or lapsed city enforcement.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints filed last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3900% spike, z-score 14.74—highest in dataset)
Virtually no complaints in prior 8-week period, indicating sudden emergence
May correlate with active development projects or street-level political/commercial campaigns
reporting_angles: Canvas Lower East Side and Chinatown storefronts: what messages are being posted? Who is behind the campaign? (political, commercial, graffiti crews?)
Interview Sanitation Dept enforcement: have they paused poster removal, or is enforcement outmatched by volume?

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Vandalism or Removal
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints jumped to 5 last week from a 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 6.29), potentially indicating infrastructure vandalism, installation errors from recent construction, or enforcement breakdown.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints filed last week vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 6.29)
Coincides with illegal tree damage spike and active construction permits (586 alteration filings in 90 days)
May indicate construction contractors removing signage without replacing or incorrect DOT coordination
reporting_angles: Map which intersections are missing signs: are they clustered on Allen Street (active ULURP projects) or near demolition/alteration sites?
Contact DOT and DOB to determine whether missing signs are from new construction projects or vandalism; check work permits against complaint locations.

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Water conservation complaints increased to 4 this week versus a 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 7.0), possibly signaling either a city-wide water emergency directive or widespread tenant reports of inadequate water supply affecting daily life.
evidence: 4 water conservation complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 7.0)
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for sanitary sewer improvements (recurring multi-year ask to DEP)
Suggests either emergency water conservation order or tenant complaints about inadequate service pressure/volume
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP: is there an active water conservation advisory or emergency in CD 103? What is the cause?
Interview residents about water pressure, supply interruptions, or building-level boiler/storage failures in the affected complaints.
